candidates.reason: Directly unit-tests ScrapyJSONEncoder.default in scrapy/utils/serialize.py. test_encode_decode asserts the exact strings produced for datetime, date and time values, so the switch from strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S') to an ISO 8601 representation changes the expected datetime value from '2010-01-02 10:11:12' to '2010-01-02T10:11:12'. This is the primary FAIL_TO_PASS coverage for the feature.

JsonLinesItemExporter and JsonItemExporter in scrapy/exporters.py serialize items with ScrapyJSONEncoder, so they inherit the new temporal format. Their test_nonstring_types_item assertions compare the exported datetime against str(datetime(2015, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)) ('2015-01-01 01:01:01'), which becomes the ISO 8601 '2015-01-01T01:01:01' after the change; the shared _get_nonstring_types_item fixture defines that value.
